from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine a double-napped cone sliced by a plane.",
            "The cutting angle determines the shape of the slice.",
            "We get circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Plane-Cone Intersection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=3).set_color(WHITE)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*2+UP*1, RIGHT*2+UP*1, RIGHT*2+DOWN*1, LEFT*2+DOWN*1).set_color("#FF9900")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(cone, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), FadeIn(plane))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Placeholder animation for "cutting angle"
        self.play(Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6, about_point=self.grid['D5']))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Show intersection curve
        curve = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FF00").move_to(self.grid['D5'])
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

class Cone(VGroup):
    def __init__(self, base_radius=1, height=2, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        # Simple 2D representation of a double-napped cone
        self.add(
            Polygon(UP*height, LEFT*base_radius+DOWN*height, RIGHT*base_radius+DOWN*height, color=WHITE),
            Polygon(DOWN*height, LEFT*base_radius+UP*height, RIGHT*base_radius+UP*height, color=WHITE)
        )

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Pick a point on our ellipse.", "Distance to foci equals segment length.", "Sums of these lengths stay constant.", "This proves the classic ellipse definition.", "The geometry is beautiful and simple."]

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", [
            "Conic sections appear in nature everywhere.",
            "From orbital paths to architectural acoustics.",
            "Dandelin spheres reveal their hidden logic."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a Whispering Gallery room layout
        room = Ellipse(width=4.0, height=2.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(room, "A4", "D6")
        self.add(room)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate sound waves bouncing between two elliptical focal points
        f1 = Dot(point=room.get_center() + LEFT*1.2, color="#FF9900")
        f2 = Dot(point=room.get_center() + RIGHT*1.2, color="#FF9900")
        
        wave = Line(f1.get_center(), room.get_edge_center(UP), color="#FF9900")
        wave2 = Line(room.get_edge_center(UP), f2.get_center(), color="#FF9900")
        
        self.add(f1, f2, wave, wave2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")
        self.play(Create(wave), Create(wave2))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out to show orbital mechanics planetary paths
        self.play(FadeOut(room), FadeOut(wave), FadeOut(wave2), FadeOut(f1), FadeOut(f2))
        orbit = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=1.5, color="#3399FF")
        planet = Dot(color="#3399FF")
        sun = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(orbit, "A4", "D6")
        self.place_at_grid(sun, "B5")
        planet.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(orbit.point_from_proportion((self.time*0.5)%1)))
        
        self.add(orbit, planet, sun)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3399FF")
        self.wait(4)

outline.topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Visualizing Conic Sections
outline.target_audience: High school students or undergraduate geometry students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Plane-Cone Intersection
sections.content: Briefly define a double-napped cone and a cutting plane. Introduce the four classic conic sections (circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) based on the angle of the cutting plane relative to the cone's axis.
sections.example: Visualizing a flashlight beam: shining it on a wall at different angles to create different shapes.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Define Dandelin spheres as the spheres inscribed within the cone, tangent to both the cone and the cutting plane. Explain that the points of tangency are the 'secret keys' to understanding the conic curves.
sections.example: An animation showing a glass cone with a floating sphere being 'squeezed' until it touches the internal surface and the flat cutting plane.

sections.title: Geometric Proof: The Ellipse Case
sections.content: Explain why the sum of distances from any point P on the ellipse to the two foci (the points of tangency) is constant. Use the property that tangent segments to a sphere from a point are equal in length.
sections.example: A rabbit moving along an elliptical track where the distance to two 'magical carrots' (foci) always adds up to the length of the cone's slant height.

sections.title: Generalizing to Parabola and Hyperbola
sections.content: Show how the placement of the sphere changes for other conics. For a parabola, only one sphere is used; for a hyperbola, the plane cuts both nappes of the cone, requiring spheres in each.
sections.example: A drone flight path (hyperbola) defined by the difference in distance between two satellite stations (the foci).

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Conclude by connecting the abstract spheres to physical optics and orbital mechanics, reinforcing that geometry is the language of nature.
sections.example: The 'Whispering Gallery' effect in architecture, where sound waves (following elliptical paths) bounce from one focal point to another.
